*** SPRINT 74 / V0.29.29 IS COMPLETE -- US-554 DONE (committed). 8 of 8 stories pass. There is NO remaining code work in this sprint; everything still open is a HARDWARE READ or a HUMAN RATIFY, listed at the bottom. Next session should expect a NEW sprint from PM, not more of this one. ***

WHAT LANDED: the ralph.sh preflight can now self-heal BL-032's lock. The guard used to refuse ANY non-empty index.lock, and BL-032's was 376467 bytes -- a crashed `git` that wrote the whole index into index.lock and died before the atomic rename. SIZE CANNOT TELL THAT ORPHAN FROM A LIVE MID-WRITE (both are big), so a size-only rule had to refuse both, and that refusal cost this sprint two uncommitted stories and a manual PM clear. The new evidence is CHANGE OVER TIME: sample (st_size, st_mtime_ns), wait ~1.5s, sample again. Identical => nothing is writing it => clearable. Different => live writer => still REFUSED_NONEMPTY.

*** THE THING I ADDED THAT NO AC ASKED FOR, AND IT IS THE PART WORTH CARRYING FORWARD: the settle interval is a ~1.5s WINDOW THAT DID NOT EXIST BEFORE. The old guard probed for a live git process and deleted immediately; now there is real time between the check and the unlink, so a git can START inside that window and be live at the moment we delete. AC-2 said the live-git gate stays 'unchanged' -- and leaving the code unchanged would have been a REGRESSION, because the gate is the same but what it guards moved. GENERALIZE: ADDING LATENCY BETWEEN A CHECK AND THE ACTION IT AUTHORIZES CREATES A TIME-OF-CHECK/TIME-OF-USE GAP, even when you add no new logic. The invariant is re-asserted after the settle; the test asserts probes==2 so it cannot pass by simply never re-probing. ***

GATE ORDER (git-live, then too-fresh, then stability) is pinned BY ABSENCE OF WORK, not just by outcome: the refusal tests assert `settled == []`, i.e. the expensive probe was never entered. An outcome-only assertion goes green on a rearrangement that lets a too-fresh lock reach the probe -- it still returns REFUSED_TOO_FRESH, while having quietly put a fresh lock on a code path that can delete. The empty-lock path never settles either, so the common preflight case costs nothing.

THE PAIR, NOT THE SIZE: the probe compares (size, mtime_ns) together. A writer rewriting the same byte count slips past a size-only compare; a coarse-granularity filesystem hides a same-second mtime move that size would catch. Both are gated, and the mtime test sets mtime EXPLICITLY with os.utime rather than by touching the file, so it does not depend on the share's clock resolution to fail. The 'still changing' tests drive the mutation through the REAL FILESYSTEM from inside the injected settleSleep -- which is precisely what a live writer looks like from the guard's side -- instead of stubbing stat.

*** TWO EXISTING TESTS WERE REPOINTED, NOT DELETED, AND THAT IS THE HONEST RECORD: test_clearStaleIndexLock_nonEmptyLock_refusesAndKeepsLock and test_backoff_nonEmpty_isTerminalNoSpin planted a STATIC non-empty lock and asserted refusal -- they pinned exactly the behaviour this story removes. They now plant a GROWING lock. The refusal survives on its new grounds (change, not size). When a story FLIPS a pinned behaviour, MOVE THE PIN and say so; deleting the test erases the record of what changed and of who agreed to it. ***

*** AC-4 WAS THE ONE AC THAT COULD HAVE SHIPPED UNFALSIFIABLE, so I gated the WIRING as well as the unit. NOTHING in the tree asserted that ralph.sh still CALLS this module -- delete the preflight line and all 34 unit tests stay green while the loop receives no fix whatsoever (US-540-b's lesson, one layer up). The new guard strips COMMENTS FIRST, because the preflight sits under a long comment block that also names the module: an unstripped scan finds the module name in PROSE and reports wiring that is not there. It asserts the invocation was FOUND before judging its shape, then asserts it does not pass --no-stable-nonempty. ***

DEFAULT IS ON in BOTH the library and the CLI (--no-stable-nonempty opts out). The AC only required the bare CLI to heal, but a library default that disagrees with its own CLI is how the next caller gets surprised. Blast radius CHECKED, not assumed: `git grep -l index_lock -- '*.py' '*.sh'` returns the module, its tests, and ralph.sh -- nothing else calls it. GOTCHA: the settle sleep had to be named settleSleep, NOT sleep -- clearStaleIndexLockWithBackoff already owns `sleep` for its retry ladder and does not forward it, so the obvious name would have silently bound the settle to the backoff.

TDD, RED TWICE ON PURPOSE: run 1 was an ImportError, which masks every per-test reason. I landed ONLY the skeleton (constant + enum member + inert params) and re-ran to get 9 BEHAVIOURAL reds, each failing because the probe was absent rather than because a name was. The other new tests were green before and after BY DESIGN -- they are the BOUND on the change (refusals that must survive it), not descriptions of it; their non-vacuity rides on the headline test proving this exact call path CAN return CLEARED_STABLE_NONEMPTY.

*** MYPY WAS NOT RUN: it is NOT INSTALLED here (`No module named mypy`) -- the same class of gap as `make` not being on PATH, and worth adding to the environment list below. AC-5 asks for mypy clean and I will not report a tool clean that I could not execute. CLAUDE.md scopes typechecking to `mypy src/` and this file is under offices/, so it is probably outside the configured surface anyway; PM to confirm at integration. RUFF IS CLEAN on both touched .py. ***

*** PRE-EXISTING RED IN tests/pm -- FILED AS TD-081, AND THE NEXT AGENT SHOULD KNOW BEFORE FENCING THERE: tests/pm/test_prd_to_sprint.py has TWO permanently-failing tests (KeyError 'bigDoDHash'). Commit 22f65a8 retired the freeze mechanic and stopped prd_to_sprint stamping frozenAt/bigDoDHash; the producer went, the tests stayed. NOT MINE (verified against my diff, not assumed). I filed rather than fixed -- PM-owned process scripts, and deleting a PM process test on my own authority is wrong even when git history is unambiguous. The real cost is not two reds: A STANDING RED TRAINS AGENTS TO READ RED AS NORMAL, and I spent a step proving it was not mine. ***

LEFT ALONE DELIBERATELY, FLAGGED: REFUSED_NONEMPTY is still TERMINAL in the backoff wrapper. Post-US-554 it means 'a write is actively in progress', which is arguably now the MOST waitable outcome there is -- but AC-2 says it stays REFUSED_NONEMPTY, an existing test pins the no-spin behaviour, and making it waitable is a design change no AC authorizes. Candidate follow-up, not drift.

PROSE REPOINTED (my own recurring lesson -- when you change a behaviour, GREP FOR THE TEXT THAT DESCRIBED IT): the module docstring's condition 3 said 'Empty (0 bytes)' full stop; ralph.sh's preflight comment said the helper 'clears ONLY a lock that is 0-byte'; the backoff docstring said a non-empty lock 'won't cure by waiting'. All three were the authoritative description of the rule this story changed.

GATE RUN SYNCHRONOUSLY IN-LOOP: tests/pm/test_index_lock.py + tests/lint = 135 collected, 134 passed, 1 skipped, exit 0, zero F/E, zero xfail. The WIDER fence (full tests/pm + tests/lint) is green EXCEPT the two TD-081 reds described above. index_lock's own file went 19 -> 34 tests (+15). ruff clean on both touched .py. No src/ or UI code touched.

ENVIRONMENT (all still true, plus two): `make` is NOT on PATH -- exits 127, WHICH READS LIKE A PASS; use `python -m ruff check <file>`. **NEW: `mypy` is NOT installed at all.** **NEW: a bash command containing `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is REFUSED ('Contains expansion') -- redirect to a file and use a plain `echo $?` on the next line.** A `tests/pm + tests/lint` run EXCEEDS 420s on this share and gets silently AUTO-BACKGROUNDED (TD-059); it still completed inside the iteration, but scope the fence to the file you touched plus the contract dir and it runs in a fraction of that. `pytest -q` prints NO summary line -- redirect, then `echo $?` AND `grep -cE '^(FAILED|ERROR)'`; `grep -c x <outfile>` catches a hidden xfail/xpass. The GREP TOOL CANNOT SEE specs/UI/dist/ -- use `git grep`. Glob over the repo root TIMES OUT (SMB); use `git ls-files | grep`. Scratch files go INSIDE the repo and get rm'd before committing. THE INDEX LOCK WAS CLEAR ALL SESSION and my commit went through normally.
